attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post. The linked tweet is a source he cites, but the jeopardy claim is his own.

semantics.note: 'Is in serious jeopardy' is a firm present-tense observation. The hedged regulatory-capture aside ('potentially') is rightly left out.

contract.note: Reading serious jeopardy as a substantial threat to agreement, shown by a breakdown or unresolved opposition on key provisions, is a fair, ordinary reading. It correctly says later passage does not undo an earlier threat.

evidence.note: IAPP, 15 Nov 2023: France and Germany demanded the foundation-model approach be withdrawn and Parliament ended the meeting early. A Parliament adviser put the odds of passage at 0–10% at that point.
Hogan Lovells, Dec 2023: dates the stall to 10 Nov 2023, when Germany, France and Italy opposed the rules and the Act's future became uncertain.

reviews.rationale: Two independent sources, both published before the evaluation date, show talks broke down on 10 Nov 2023 over foundation models, with major member states opposed and a participant putting the odds of passage at 0–10%. That meets the support condition. The later December deal does not contradict an observation of jeopardy at that time.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: The phrase is an evaluative aside describing the Act, not a measurable comparison. 'Closest thing we have' and 'real teeth' come with no metric, no set of comparators and no weighting.

contract.note: The contract admits the result depends on how breadth, enforceability and in-force status are weighed, and on which jurisdictions are compared. Marcus supplied none of this, so any verdict would rest on the evaluator's own choice of weighting.

evidence.note: June 2023 Parliament draft amendments on penalties and redress. They show an enforcement component but no comparative standing.
Clifford Chance describes the proposed fines (up to 7% of turnover) and an AI office. Shows substantial proposed powers, not a ranking.
China's generative AI measures, in force since Aug 2023, with suspension and penalty powers. Narrower in scope; a possible comparator but not decisive.
Fact sheet on the US executive order's reporting requirements. A comparator of different legal character; it does not settle the ranking.

reviews.rationale: 'Closest thing we have to AI regulation with real teeth' is an evaluative description with no stated measure. Whether the EU draft or China's in-force but narrower rules come out ahead depends entirely on a weighting Marcus never gave, as the contract itself admits. The claim is too evaluative to score fairly.
